pull_request.title: Infrastructure: pick up reviewer-labeled agent tasks hourly on mac-studio-01
pull_request.head: codex/hourly-agent-tasks
pull_request.body:
## Executive summary

Reviewers can now queue bounded work by applying `agent_task` to an open issue or same-repository PR. This PR adds an hourly macOS LaunchAgent for `acts-mac-studio-01`, a poller that attempts one new request per tick, and deployment instructions. The GitHub label has already been created, and `asalzburger-review` was verified to have write access.

The scheduler is **not loaded**. Review and merge first, then deploy from a stable checkout using [the operations guide](tools/agent_tasks/README.md). Loading starts an immediate check as well as checks at minute 7 each hour. The macOS user must be logged in, and the Mac awake and online.

## Change

- Accept requests labeled by `asalzburger-review` or `asalzburger`; support issues and same-repository PRs, including PR review context.
- Use the label event ID for durable deduplication. Removing/reapplying the label requests a fresh attempt; comments and failed/interrupted attempts do not automatically repeat.
- Recheck queued requests, lock out overlapping workers, cap each run at 3300 seconds, and use a separate worktree at the latest main/captured PR head.
- Run Codex with `workspace-write` and no interactive approval. Leave local changes and final results for human review; the initial runner does not publish changes, comment, mutate labels, merge or grant sign-off.
- Add queue tests to CI and document authentication, deployment, sleep/logout behavior, failures, retries and shutdown.

This is repository infrastructure under the existing ADR-003/ADR-004 policies; both ADRs remain DRAFT. No detector parameters, scientific provenance, project progress entries or sign-off states change. The user confirmed that both issues and PRs should be supported.

## Dashboard and validation

- [x] Infrastructure PR: no maintenance entries added to scientific progress tracking.
- [x] 15 queue tests pass, including real local Git fetch/worktree creation with a fake Codex executable, deduplication, cancellation/relabel races, failed attempts, locking, PR head changes, fork filtering and timeout cleanup.
- [x] Live read-only GitHub dry-run succeeds on mac-studio-01; no eligible tasks and no task started.
- [x] Generated LaunchAgent passes `plutil -lint`; no live scheduler loaded and no paid model call used for testing.
- [x] Project records validate and the token dashboard builds.
- [x] Session records validate; staged diff and new Git objects inspected, with no large run artifacts or credentials.
- [x] Individual PR interaction record synchronized and validated.
- [x] Human approval boundaries preserved; layout and detector validation unaffected.

Curated session: `SESSION-2026-11-06-hourly-agent-tasks`. Exact token counters for the active session are unavailable; no usage was estimated.

events.text:
Created the GitHub `agent_task` label (purple `6F42C1`) with the requested queue
meaning. GitHub CLI confirmed `asalzburger-review` has write access. No repository
permission was changed. The connector's collaborator permission endpoint returned
403, so the authenticated GitHub CLI was used for that read and label creation.

Added a Python standard-library poller and explicit LaunchAgent generator. The
schedule is once hourly at minute 7 and at load, restricted to the verified host
`acts-mac-studio-01`. The allowlist contains the established reviewer and repository
publishing accounts. One task is attempted per tick, using a separate worktree.
Each label event is claimed durably before starting; repeated ticks, comments and
failed/interrupted attempts do not duplicate execution. Removing/reapplying the
label requests a fresh attempt. A local lock prevents overlapping workers using
the same state directory. This is not a distributed queue.

Both issues and same-repository PRs are supported. PRs include public review
context and are tied to the captured head revision; external-fork PRs are skipped.
Codex uses `workspace-write` and never requests interactive approval. The prompt
requires repository governance, tests and curated reporting, and leaves local
changes/results for human review without pushing, publishing, commenting, label
mutation, merging or human sign-off. Missing permissions remain blockers.

The generator writes a reviewable plist with absolute executable paths and shell
PATH but never loads a job. No live scheduler or paid Codex task was started in
this implementation session. Deployment after merge uses the documented stable
checkout, logged-in macOS user and existing CLI authentication. Sleeping/offline
machines cannot provide an exact wall-clock hourly service.
